report:
### Executive Summary
The image features a tourist-style "forced perspective" photograph of the iconic Stone Chariot located at the Vitthala Temple complex in Hampi, Karnataka, India. The photographer is aligning the physical monument with its illustration on a modern Indian 50-Rupee note. The identity of the landmark is confirmed through architectural consistency and the direct correlation between the monument and the currency.

### Image Summary
A first-person perspective shot showing a hand holding a 50-Indian Rupee note in the foreground. The note is positioned to overlap with the iconic stone chariot structure in the background, which is situated in an open, sunlit archaeological courtyard.

### Primary Subject
The Stone Chariot, a granite architectural masterpiece serving as a secondary shrine within the Vitthala Temple complex.

### Directly Observed Clues
*   **Stone Chariot:** A monolithic-looking structure with granite wheels, an ornate superstructure, and elephant sculptures at the base.
*   **Currency:** A modern Indian 50-Rupee note featuring the Stone Chariot as its primary motif.
*   **Surroundings:** Stone-paved courtyard, colonnaded halls, and a prominent temple tower (gopuram) in the distance.
*   **Environment:** Arid, hilly backdrop and high-intensity sunlight creating a lens flare.

### Inferred Findings
The photographer is participating in a common tourist tradition of aligning official currency with the real-world monument. The architectural style (Dravidian) and the presence of protective barriers suggest a site managed for cultural heritage preservation.

### Probable Location
The Vitthala Temple complex, Hampi, Karnataka, India.

### Landmark Identification
The Stone Chariot, Hampi.

### Location Confidence
Very High. The unique iconography of the wheels and the specific chariot design match both historical records and the depiction on the legal tender used in the photo.

### Authenticity Assessment
The image appears to be a genuine, unaltered photograph. The alignment is a common photographic technique and shows no signs of digital editing or synthesis.

### Historical and Cultural Context
Built during the Vijayanagara Empire (roughly 15th–16th century), the structure is a shrine historically dedicated to Garuda. It is located within the Vitthala Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its "musical pillars" and grand Dravidian architecture.

### Reasoning and Alternative Hypotheses
The identification is supported by the visual match between the monument and the 50-Rupee note, which is known to feature this specific landmark. There are no competing hypotheses, as the visual evidence is self-verifying.

### Additional Observations
The sunlight suggests the photo was taken during daylight hours. The visible barriers indicate the site is under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

### Verification Status
The identification of the site as the Stone Chariot in the Vitthala Temple complex is supported by multiple sources:
*   *Stone Chariot - Karnataka Tourism* (https://karnatakatourism.org/en/attractions/stone-chariot)
*   *Stone Chariot, Vitthala Temple | Sculpture & Installation* (https://imp-art.org/articles/stone-chariot-vitthala-temple/)
*   *Vittala Temple | Temples in Hampi | Hampi* (https://www.karnataka.com/hampi/vittala-temple/)
*   *Musical Pillars & Stone Chariot at Vitthala Temple in Hampi* (https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/karnataka/hampi/vitthala-temple-complex)

### Uncertainties
There is zero uncertainty regarding the identity of the monument. Minor uncertainty remains regarding the exact date of the photo, though it must be after 2017 when the current 50-Rupee note design was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India.

The massive sculpture of Garuda, Lord Vishnu’s escort, once was seated atop the chariot but it is empty at the present date. Mar 10, 2026 · Although it appears to be carved from a single rock, the chariot is actually a small temple constructed using several large granite blocks assembled with remarkable precision.
